name: Kimodo SOMA RP v1.1
description: NVIDIA Kimodo trained on Bones Rigplay. Starts exactly from the current pose.

code.install: Install Kimodo into ComfyUI's Python environment: 'pip install git+https://github.com/nv-tlabs/kimodo', then restart ComfyUI. The text encoder uses the gated meta-llama/Meta-Llama-3-8B-Instruct model: request access on Hugging Face and run 'hf auth login' once. See docs/VNCCS_POSE_STUDIO_TEXT_TO_MOTION.md.

requirements.notes: Most of the memory is the LLM2Vec text encoder. Set TEXT_ENCODER_DEVICE=cpu to keep it on the CPU; the motion model itself needs under 3 GB.

guide.summary: Recommended. Starts exactly from the pose you made, so the clip continues it naturally. Realistic human motion, up to 10 s.
guide.best_for: Continuing your pose; walking, gestures, sports, everyday actions
guide.setup_effort: Easy: one Install button plus a one-time Hugging Face access request

setup.label: Kimodo Python package
setup.detail: Installed with ComfyUI-Manager. Kimodo requires transformers 5.1.0, which replaces the version in ComfyUI's Python.

setup.label: Access to Meta Llama 3 8B Instruct (gated)
setup.detail: Kimodo's text encoder is built on Meta Llama 3. Open the model page, accept the license with your Hugging Face account, then log in once from ComfyUI's Python environment.

setup.label: Model and text encoder (~17 GB)
setup.detail: Downloaded by Kimodo itself on the first generation, so the first run takes a while.
